title: RS_ReplaceBandNoDataValue
description: >
  Moves a band's nodata value to a new value, carrying the nodata pixels with
  it: every pixel that reads as nodata is rewritten to the new value, which then
  becomes the band's nodata, so the same pixels read as nodata before and after.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: band
      type: int
      description: Band index (1-based).
    - name: nodata
      type: float64
      description: >
        The new nodata value. It must fit the band's data type exactly.
---

## Description

`RS_SetBandNoDataValue` changes only the declared nodata value, so pixels that
held the old value become ordinary data. `RS_ReplaceBandNoDataValue` also
rewrites those pixels, so they keep reading as nodata.

A pixel reads as nodata by the same rules sampling uses: exactly for integer
bands, and numerically for float bands, so `-0.0` matches a `0.0` nodata and
any NaN matches a NaN nodata. Other bands are unchanged.

The band must already have a nodata value; otherwise there is nothing to
replace and the call is an error. A null raster, band or nodata value gives a
null raster. Only 2-D rasters are supported.

## Examples

Band 1 of `RS_Example()` has a nodata value of 127, held by one of its 2048
pixels. Replacing the nodata value keeps that pixel as nodata, so 2047 pixels
stay valid; merely setting a new nodata value with `RS_SetBandNoDataValue`
turns it into ordinary data, leaving 2048 valid:

```sql
SELECT
  RS_SummaryStats(RS_ReplaceBandNoDataValue(RS_Example(), 1, 200), 'count', 1),
  RS_SummaryStats(RS_SetBandNoDataValue(RS_Example(), 1, 200), 'count', 1);
```

```sql
SELECT RS_BandNoDataValue(RS_ReplaceBandNoDataValue(RS_Example(), 1, 200), 1);
```
